beliefs.statement: Constant heights (a single box) give R=2/3 because f*f is triangular.

R is large when f*f is flat and rectangle-like with a suppressed peak. A symmetric f can achieve this as well as an asymmetric one (symmetrizing p0012 retained R=0.833835), so asymmetry is NOT required — the lever is peak suppression / flatness of f*f, not f's asymmetry.

Every 'plateau' so far (0.8410, 0.8426, 0.8432, 0.8524) has been a recipe artifact, not a problem limit: the tiny-N global search plus restart polish has now reached 0.856207 (p0076) and 0.855549 (p0079).
Direct height-vector optimization from smooth or flat-top seeds reaches R≥0.80, far above any fixed parametric family (best family 0.7437).
Flat-topped f produce flat-topped, more rectangle-like f*f, raising R above the Gaussian's 0.7071.

A monotone exponential tilt h*exp(lambda*(2x-1)) with lambda around 1, followed by block reoptimization, gives a large gain on the p0004 line (0.807751 to 0.833835); multi-scale refinement from a symmetric seed also reaches 0.829953.

Targeted dip suppression, mass-preserving progressive upsampling to N=20000-40000 with per-level block refinement, fine-block (2-6) polishing, and restarts are complementary and compose: p0038 0.840911, p0043 0.840536, p0045 0.840995, p0049 0.840961.

Mirror symmetry about the center is a severe restriction at high resolution: forcing symmetry drives f*f's max to the center (Cauchy-Schwarz) and collapses the score (p0070: symmetrized p0066 fell to 0.715 vs 0.8426 free).

High-N is saturated: resampling p0045 to N=60000 and N=80000 with the fast incremental block-1/2 optimizer gains only +0.000002 (p0053). N=40000 is the practical resolution ceiling; extra N buys nothing.
Random smooth additive bump perturbations of the height vector (p0023) add only ~0.0006, well below targeted multiplicative dips; they are not a strong structural lever.
Fine block sizes (2-6) with decaying steps plus narrow Gaussian dips (widths 0.002-0.06) at N=4000-40000 give real gains: p0029 +0.0007, p0034 +0.0004, p0040 +0.0002, p0043 +0.0003, p0049 +0.00005.
An early short fine local polish, a tightened dip scan, and restarts that grow N toward 4000 give a big gain on p0025 (p0026 0.839812, p0027 0.839798).
Target-driven deconvolution of a flat-top f*f target (p0041) scores only 0.791, far below direct height optimization; it is not a competitive construction region.

Exact incremental O(N*b) delta-convolution scoring makes block-1/2 descent affordable at N=40000 but yields only +0.000004 over p0045's coarse-block ascent (p0054): the full-convolution scorer was NOT the bottleneck, so the plateau is a property of the shape, not of the optimizer's cost.

f*f is always symmetric about the center of f's support. If f is symmetric about 0.5 then f*f's maximum is at the center; the best solutions instead peak at 0.54-0.57 of support, consistent with f being approximately symmetric about a shifted center c~0.55-0.57 (support roughly [2c-1,1]). This is why mirror symmetry about 0.5 is limiting and shifted symmetry about a free c is the right reduced parametrization.
Low-N (N~1000-2500) height vectors with noisy block restarts + N growth keep paying: p0069 added +0.000588 to p0066 (0.843206), confirming the restart recipe is not saturated on a good basin.

Scaling the tiny-N global search keeps paying: N0=250/250 inits gave 0.852421 (p0072), and N0=320/400 inits with top-15 upscale gave 0.856207 (p0076) — tiny stage 0.852331, upscale +0.0017, restarts +0.0022. The basin landscape is rich and unsaturated.

The p0066 basin scores high with a much flatter f (max/mean 2.59) and a flatter f*f peak (7.56% of knots within 0.1% of max) than the p0057 line (max/mean 4.08, 1.12%), with the f*f max at 0.443 (left of center); this suggests a broad flat f*f top, not a sharp peak, is what raises R.
The tiny-N global search is far from saturated: going from N0=250/250 inits to N0=320/400 inits gained +0.0038 (p0076). Both the tiny stage and the upscale+restart stages contributed substantially.

A dedicated long noisy-restart + block-ascent polish of a good basin (p0072) gains a lot: +0.00313 to 0.855549 (p0079), with the restart stage alone contributing +0.00287. Restart polish is not saturated.

Cheap single-coordinate polish followed by alternating refine/noisy-restart with downscale-relocate gains +0.00238 on p0072 (p0077, mutation loop), confirming coordinate polish is a cheap high-value stage.

summary.text: Current best is 0.840999 (p0052). R is maximized by nonnegative f whose convolution is flat and rectangle-like with a suppressed peak; symmetry is not required. Next tests: escape the plateau via randomized basin hopping, test high-N mirror symmetry, and try a multi-lobe construction from scratch.

beliefs.statement: p0001's uniform 50-step construction scores R=2/3; since only shape matters, this is the uniform-block baseline.
A single uniform block has a triangular autoconvolution, so its R is exactly 2/3; beating it requires non-uniform heights that make f*f less triangular/more plateau-like.
Multi-level equal-width blocks remain the strongest region: K=6 at N=800 reaches 0.8577 (p0018) while the best smooth/spline family (p0014) tops out at 0.8421 even under a full-budget challenge.
Optimizing K=4 equal-width block heights with differential evolution reaches R=0.8444, far above the uniform 2/3 and the smooth 0.787.
Higher R correlates with a broader near-max f*f plateau: p0035 (38.06% within 0.1%, R=0.857843) > p0034 (37.98%, 0.857833) > p0024 (27.98%, 0.857008).
Local hill-climbing from the uniform shape is a weak route: p0006 reached only 0.7583, while direct block optimization reached 0.8444.

Best recipe: K=6 equal-width staircase -> resample -> Gaussian smooth with sigma ~1.5-3 grid steps -> exact-R L-BFGS-B, repeated. Reaches 0.858176 (p0079). The recipe is now exhausted: N=6400 ladders, two-pass sigma, structural perturbations and restarts all add <1e-5.
Free-width block parametrization is a weak route: global DE K=8 (p0036, +3e-6) and local free-width K=6 refinement of the equal-width shape (p0042, +0) both fail to beat equal-width K=6.
Equal-width block optimization saturates at K=6: K=7..12 local continuations gave zero (p0018, p0020) and a genuinely global K=9 DE/NM search also gave zero (p0037).
For equal-width blocks at N=800 the K=6 shape is a local optimum in K, so further gains must come from coordinate/gradient polish or higher resolution, not more blocks.
The block-staircase family is near a ceiling: best is 0.858176 (p0079). Non-block routes (Gaussian mixture p0076 0.853978, multi-family random search p0078 0.854690) stay 3-4e-3 below.

Resolution beyond N=3200 is not a lever on the block basin (N=6400 ladder +6e-6 p0073, +4e-6 p0079), but it IS a lever on the non-block Gaussian-mixture line (N=6400 gave +1.9e-4, p0076). Resolution tests must be basin-specific.

Perturb+polish at N=3200 on the already-polished block basin adds at most ~1e-5 (p0072 0/3, p0073 0/2, p0077 0/1 improved). The lever is resolution/polish-state dependent: on an under-polished N=1600 profile, 15 perturb restarts gave +1.5e-3 (p0078).

The single-argmax inf-norm makes the objective non-smooth at the optimum, which limits exact-R gradient/coordinate methods; an annealed p-norm surrogate (||L||_p, p→∞) warm-started from the same point can reach a slightly better R than exact-R polish.

The optimal Gaussian sigma is ~2-3 grid steps at N=6400 (~1.5 at N=3200). A second sigma pass at N=3200 on the block basin adds only 5.4e-6 (p0072), while it adds +5.0e-4 on the non-block Gaussian-mixture basin (p0071): repeated sigma passes are basin-specific.
Neither annealed p-norm homotopy (p=4..1e4) nor flat-target deconvolution escapes the plateau: p0048 gave 0 gain over 0.857844 and p0049 landed at 0.815070.

Smoothing is a general polish, not basin-locked: it lifted p0033's line by +3.0e-4 (p0058) and the Gaussian-mixture line by +1.3e-3 (p0064), while already-polished arrays (p0048, p0051) gain 0. The size of the gain depends on how under-smoothed the basin is.

The non-block Gaussian-mixture line (p0057->p0064->p0071->p0076) is a distinct basin (f*f max at 0.61, linf 0.8248) whose N=3200 sigma lever saturated but whose resolution lever did not: N=6400 gave +1.9e-4 to 0.853978. It is still 4e-3 below the block best.

The block-staircase basin is exhausted near 0.8582: budget-aware N=6400 ladder +6e-6 (p0073), two-pass sigma +9e-6 (p0072), low-frequency structural perturbations +2e-6 (p0077), extra N=6400 pass +4e-6 (p0079). Further gains require a structurally different profile, not more polishing.

Across the top constructions ||f*f||_2^2 (unit mass on [0,1]) is pinned at ~0.7037-0.7044 (p0077 0.703957, p0079 0.703743, p0076 0.704361), so R ~= 0.704/linf and any new record must come from lowering ||f*f||_inf below 0.8200 rather than from raising the L2 mass.

summary.text: Best is 0.858086 (p0054): K=6 equal-width staircase, fine Gaussian smoothing, exact-R polish. Coarse sigma=0.5 was suboptimal; fine sigma is a real lever. Resolution beyond N=3200, K>6, free-width blocks, coordinate descent, p-norm homotopy and flat-target deconvolution have all failed to add. The open tests are whether p0054 survives N=6400, whether smoothing transfers to the p0048 basin, and whether a from-scratch spectral continuous profile can escape the block family. The block-staircase region remains dominant but the ceiling is not yet proved.

beliefs.statement: The constant step function with 50 equal heights has R = 2/3 exactly.
Peaked non-flat shapes vastly exceed 2/3: free-form optimized bumps climb from 0.72 to 0.90 as the optimizer improves (p0003 0.840, p0023 0.873, p0030 0.9045).
A peaked (non-flat) f makes f*f fuller near its maximum relative to ||f*f||_inf, raising R while ||f*f||_1 is fixed by scaling.

Symmetry is not a disadvantage: symmetric-constrained optimization matches the asymmetric 0.841166 exactly. Yet the current best (p0019, 0.842478) has its f*f maximum at 0.355 of support, so mild asymmetry appears at the top.

Resolution alone gives little: pure N=3200 softmax ascent from p0030 gained exactly 0.000000 (p0037). Gains come from escaping the basin at fixed N by re-heating (+0.00263, p0034) or by coarsening then re-ascending (+0.00122, p0036).
The optimum is a single dense bump, not sparse/comb: p0029's sparse/comb/multi-hump search from scratch reached only 0.8353, far below the dense 0.9045.

Hard-max local ascent saturates ~0.844; analytic-gradient softmax ascent is the dominant lever (p0030 +0.031, p0035 +0.0398 in the mutation loop, p0034 +0.0026 on top of it). Gradient speed alone is not enough.

Softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever; re-heating T to ~1e-3*maxL after annealing to 1e-6-1e-7*maxL escapes the local basin. T_hi=1e-3*maxL is near-optimal: the p0054 sweep gained +1.4e-4 with no evidence a T_hi outside [3e-4,3e-3] won, and p0055's standard-T reheat gained +3.7e-4.

The best construction p0043 is a peaked f (max/mean 13.14, 41.1% zeros) with a flat-topped asymmetric f*f: 41.79% of knots within 5% of max, 28.29% within 0.1%, max at 0.302 of support, ||f*f||_inf=0.871268. The f*f max location is not stable across high scorers (0.302 p0043, 0.373 p0042, 0.524 p0040), so it is not a reliable design target.

R is driven by making f*f flat over a wide region while keeping sup low: p0043 has 41.79% of knots within 5% of max (28.29% within 0.1%) and scores 0.907570; p0040 with 41.46% within 5% scores 0.904962.
Analytic softmax gradients with higher N gained +0.031 over 0.873353 in one run (p0030), confirming the prediction by a wide margin.
The p0052 hop basin is saturated at N=800 (iid hops add 0 after cycle 1), but mass-preserving upsample to N=1600 plus reheat adds +1.06e-4 (p0058); exact hard polish remains <1e-5.
Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap but saturating escape: p0043 +4.1e-4, p0047 +3.9e-4, p0055 +3.7e-4, p0054 +1.4e-4, p0058 +1.06e-4 at N=1600.
Coarsening to N=400 and re-ascending reaches regions the N=800 ascent cannot: p0034's soft400 stage gained +0.0022 and p0036's coarsen+re-ascend gained +0.0012, both more than pure N=800 polishing.
Exact hard-max polish after a softmax anneal adds negligible gain (<1e-5): p0040 +4e-6, p0047 +6e-6, p0052 +2e-6, p0055 +2e-6.

Large multiplicative basin-hopping (sigma U(0.05,0.25), optional zeroing of the smallest 10-20%) followed by re-annealing escapes to structurally different basins: p0048 +3.3e-4 (40.8% zeros, f*f max 0.303), p0052 +4.5e-4 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373, best 0.908417).

At least three structurally different basins reach >=0.9079: p0047 (1.7% zeros, max 0.496), p0048 (40.8% zeros, max 0.303), p0052 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373); p0055 (4.5% zeros, max 0.671) may be a mirror-related basin. R is largely insensitive to zero-gap structure, so gains come from finding new basins, not refining one.
Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle 1 +4.5e-4, cycles 2-4 exactly 0; p0058 cycle 1 +1.05e-4, cycle 2 exactly 0.
Block/segment perturbations are not a better escape than iid per-step hops: p0059 gained only +1.4e-5 at N=800 vs p0052's +4.5e-4.
Structural moves on a dense bump (contiguous zero gap, added second hump) reach only 0.907274 (p0060), far below the dense single-bump best 0.908523; sparse/multi-hump structure is not competitive.

summary.text: Current best 0.908417 (p0052) is a large-sigma hop basin, about +4.5e-4 over p0047. Softmax/logsumexp analytic ascent remains the core lever; exact hard polish adds <1e-5. Fixed-N reheat saturates near +4e-4, while large multiplicative hops now give the best gains. At least three structurally different basins (p0047, p0048, p0052) score ~0.908, so R is relatively insensitive to zero gaps and f*f max location. Untested: N=1600 hopping/reheat from p0052, optimal T_hi for this basin, and whether sparse/comb shapes can challenge the dense bump. Constant function remains 2/3.
